content.content:
deccy's store is rooted at the trunk. Every invocation that touches graph state opens one store, and the root it is opened on is the trunk working copy's root — the root of the repository's own working copy, which holds the repository's `.jj` and deccy's state directory `.deccy/` — not the root of the working copy the invocation happens to run in. The invocation resolves that root from its own workspace before the store exists; the store is opened on the resolved root and holds it as the whole of what it is: one root, never a second one, no probing for another, no retry or re-open on a different root once it is open, and no reach of its own (ppwnzwwy). Which working copy the invocation runs in therefore does not move the store: a call made from a draft workspace opens the same store, on the same trunk root, as a call made from the trunk.

The trunk root is a place, not a label. It is the root of the working copy the repository belongs to, fixed by where the state directory sits: the working copy whose root contains `.deccy/`. Because it is named by that place, no change id makes a working copy the trunk, no workspace name does, and neither the name a checkout is registered under nor the change it has checked out is one of the terms: the trunk is the trunk after it is renamed and after it is checked out at a different change (uqqswnsy). A draft's workspace is another working copy of the same tree, placed under one per-user root outside the repository at the directory its handle names (xqzstoyo); its root holds no state directory, so it is not the place the trunk is, and it cannot serve as the store's root.

The trunk root is resolved from the invocation workspace. The invocation begins at its own workspace root — the root the jj seam resolves for the working copy the caller ran in — and follows that working copy's repository entry to the working copy the repository belongs to; the root of that working copy is the trunk root, and it is the root the store is opened on. Resolution happens once, before the store exists; its result is the store's only root. Nothing below the store chooses a root, and the store never chooses one after it is opened.

The jj runner does not follow the store to the trunk. The invocation keeps two roots, and they answer two different questions: the store's root is the trunk's, while the jj runner's anchor stays the invocation workspace root. Every jj command the invocation issues runs against the invocation workspace — the root `jj workspace root` yields at the invocation's own working directory, and every read and edit beneath it — so a draft invocation's jj work lands in the draft working copy, not in the trunk (xqzstoyo). Rooting the store at the trunk does not move the working copy the invocation edits; the two roots coincide only when the invocation already runs in the trunk, and that coincidence is an outcome of the place, not a rule tying the runner to the store.

Every graph-file kind an invocation opens — store read, store write, markers, exclude, and journal — is opened on the store's root, and none of them resolves a root from the invocation, the caller, or any origin of its own (xquwmsts). The marker stack, the exclude file, the journal entries and blobs, and the node documents a write places under the root all sit under the one working copy that holds `.deccy/`: the trunk. A draft workspace therefore never reads or writes the marker stack and gets no second marker file: the markers interface opens the trunk's file, so brackets land there whatever working copy the invocation runs in (uqqswnsy), and work performed in the draft workspace is not bracketed at all. There is no per-workspace and no per-interface choice of root left to make after the store is opened: the root is decided once, before the store is constructed, and each interface is handed it.

When the trunk root cannot be resolved from the invocation workspace, the invocation refuses, and the refusal names the cause it met. A refusal is the whole of what an unresolvable trunk produces: it opens nothing on the invocation workspace root, creates no state directory to manufacture a root for itself, probes no other working copy, re-opens on no other root, and does not continue with a store that has no root (ppwnzwwy, xquwmsts, xqzstoyo, uqqswnsy). The invocation root is not a fallback in any of those forms, and there is no retry that swaps one root for another: a root chosen after the refusal would be a second root, and the store holds one (ppwnzwwy).

These clauses are one commitment. The store holds one root and lends it (ppwnzwwy); that root is the place where the state directory sits, not a change or a name (uqqswnsy); the place is reached from the invocation workspace, and the refusal is what happens when it cannot be (xqzstoyo); and the jj runner stays on the invocation workspace, so the store's root and the working copy the invocation edits are two answers to two questions (xqzstoyo). Take any one away and the rest fails: give the store the invocation's root and the markers, journal and node writes of an invocation run in a draft land in a working copy that holds no state directory (uqqswnsy); let the jj runner follow the store to the trunk and a draft's jj edits land in the trunk working copy (xqzstoyo); let an unresolvable trunk fall back to the invocation root and both failures happen with no refusal to mark them (ppwnzwwy).

Not settled here: the file the invocation's repository entry is spelled as, the cases in which following it leaves the trunk unresolved, the shape of a path it names, how far it is followed, and the wording, stream and exit status of the refusal. Those belong to the resolution and to the envelope that renders a refusal, and each can change without moving what this node settles: one store, on the trunk's root, resolved from the invocation workspace, with the jj runner left where the invocation is.
content.rationale:
The store's root was the one thing left open once the four prerequisites were read: the store holds one root and lends it (ppwnzwwy), every graph-file kind is opened on that root (xquwmsts), and the marker stack belongs to one working copy named by place (uqqswnsy). None of them says which working copy's root the store is opened on, and the question matters only because a draft's workspace is a different working copy of the tree, outside the repository (xqzstoyo): a store opened on the invocation's own root would put a draft invocation's markers, journal and node writes in a tree that holds no state directory, which uqqswnsy forecloses. Rooting the store at the trunk is therefore the only root the three already describe, not a fourth rule beside them.

Rooting the store at the trunk does not decide where the invocation's jj work goes. A draft invocation must edit its own working copy, and moving the jj runner to the trunk would put a draft's jj edits in the trunk — exactly what the separate draft workspace exists to prevent (xqzstoyo). The two roots are therefore stated together, because each is the other's limit: the store is the trunk's, and the runner's anchor is the invocation's; written alone, either would invite the other to be inferred into it.

Naming the trunk by place is what makes the root survive renaming and checkout, and what makes it reachable from an invocation without a label: the invocation workspace is a working copy of the same tree, so its repository entry already says which working copy the repository belongs to, and that working copy's root is the trunk root. Resolving before the store exists and handing the result to the store keeps root choice in one place, which is what ppwnzwwy and xquwmsts require of everything below the store; resolution on demand inside the store or inside an interface would be the second root they close.

Refusal is the other half of the same rule rather than a policy beside it. If the trunk root cannot be reached from the invocation workspace, every remaining option is a root the decision has already excluded: the invocation workspace root holds no state directory (uqqswnsy), creating one would manufacture the place (xqzstoyo), and proceeding would leave the store with no root to lend (ppwnzwwy). Naming the cause makes the refusal usable — it says which step failed, so a broken draft can be told from an invocation made outside a repository — while the catalogue of causes stays with the resolution.

Left out because another node owns it: the file the repository entry is spelled as, the cases in which following it yields nothing, the path shape and how far it is followed, and the refusal's wording, stream and exit status. Each can change without moving what this node settles.
